alignments.note: Conditional particle to the word introducing the English clause (rule 40).

Inflected verb takes subject and auxiliary as helpers, headed on the lexical verb (rule 9). The preverb συν- is realized by 'together' inside the verb's own unit (rule 106); 'with' is left to the dative, since the ASV writes a particle for the preverb in addition to the case preposition.
Article before a name with no English determiner (rule 23).
The ASV gives the noun no determiner, so the case preposition 'with' stays with the noun rather than anchoring on the article (rules 21, 106).
Substantival article before an adverb: it keeps the discontinuous 'the things that', headed on the nominal word, since a bare adverb has no verb to carry the relativizer (rules 22, 32).
Adverbial predicate carries the supplied copula (rule 53).
Article before a name, no English realization (rule 23).
Expressed copula; the participle keeps its own word, so the pair splits under rule 2.
Anarthrous substantival adjective expanded with a supplied noun and determiner: helpers ride with it and the head stays on the adjective (rules 17, 51).
No English determiner for 'God', so the article anchors nothing (rules 21, 23).
Case preposition stays with the determinerless noun (rule 21).
Participle in the periphrasis; the copula is the expressed ἐστιν's.
